newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania tells U.S. elections will be clean fight.
newsitem.headline: Albania tells U.S. elections will be clean fight.

text.p: Albania said on Friday it had assured the United States it would respect democratic standards in municipal polls on October 20 after Washington expressed concern over a flawed general election in May.
The U.S. State Department has urged President Sali Berisha's conservative government to ensure the local elections are properly conducted and to guarantee an accurate count of the vote.

Foreign Minister Tritan Shehu, who returned from a visit to the United States this week, said relations between the two countries remained on a good footing, despite criticism over the conduct of the general election.
"I assured them the Albanian government had the full will to secure a normal election process and to carry it out in full transparency," Shehu told a news conference.
The United States and the European Union have said they would be watching the municipal elections closely as a test of Albania's commitment to democracy.
Most opposition parties, including the main Socialist Party, the former communists, pulled out of the May general election, accusing Berisha's Democratic Party of electoral fraud.
Foreign observers upheld many of the opposition complaints.
The conservative Democrats almost swept the board, securing 89 percent of the seats in the 140-member parliament.
U.S. diplomats in Tirana stayed away from the opening session of the newly elected parliament on July 1.
The U.S. embassy said this week that Washington had noted the progress made by the government in opening dialogue with the opposition before the local elections.
